pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Ethos & Values - Queens Park Community School
pageCache.text:
Vision, Ethos & Values
QPCS Vision
Queens Park Community School (QPCS) is a centre of academic excellence at the heart of our community, with the highest expectations for all of our students.
QPCS Ethos
At Queens Park Community School we know that our community shapes who we are.
All members of our school community are expected to be responsible, respectful and resilient.
Our students’ success is built on our ethos of high expectations for all; being community-minded; and being fair to ourselves and to others.
Fairness encompasses equality, justice, liberty and democracy.
Being community-minded involves social responsibility, co-operation and solidarity.
QPCS Values:
Building Responsible, Resilient, and Respectful Citizens
At Queens Park Community School our educational approach is centred around developing students who embody our core values of Responsibility, Resilience, and Respect. These values are integral to our curriculum, community life, and commitment to preparing students for life in modern Britain.
Our QPCS values link to British Values, which underpin what it is to be a citizen in a modern and diverse Britain. They allow us to create environments free from discrimination, intolerance and hate. They help us to challenge prejudice and stereotyping, whilst strengthening relationships within the community.
Responsibility and Student Voice
We teach our students to take responsibility for their own learning, actions, and the continuous improvement of the QPCS community.
Resilience and Individual Liberty
Students are taught to be resilient, empowering them to understand and protect their individual liberty and the rights of those around them.
Respect is fundamental to our diverse community.
Pupil voice is at the heart of decision making

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Queens Park Community School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Queens Park Community School.
As Headteacher, I am proud to lead our community, dedicated to academic excellence and high expectations for every student. Our ethos of responsibility, respect, and resilience creates a safe and challenging environment. We are proud of the expertise, quality and commitment of our teachers and support staff.
Our school badge shows that we are rooted in our community, aiming for the stars. At QPCS, it is not about where you are from – what really matters is where you are going to; and our former students demonstrate the success of our ethos. We offer a balanced curriculum with strong academic opportunities and tailored support, guiding students to success in university or vocational paths. Our mixed attainment teaching and strong home-school partnerships are evidence-based, and we know how our approach helps all students thrive. Our results demonstrate this success. Our highest attainers make great progress and achieve grade 9s at GCSE, and A* s at A Level; whilst also benefiting from truly diverse classrooms and insights into different ways of thinking.
QPCS welcomes disabled students, staff and parents and aims to make all of our provisions fully inclusive. Students with an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan are given priority in our admissions criteria. As part of the admissions procedure their families will meet with our SENCO to discuss their specific needs.
I hope you will join us at Open Evening. If you are a Year 6 parent, you are also welcome to book on to a Parent Tour during the school day.
Best wishes Ms J Enright, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Instrumental Lessons & Music Development Plan - Queens Park Community School
pageCache.text:
Instrumental Lessons & Music Development Plan
At Queens Park Community School, we believe that learning an instrument is a rewarding journey that builds confidence, creativity, and lifelong skills. We offer a diverse range of instrumental lessons, including piano, voice, guitar, drum kit, orchestral strings, brass, and woodwind, taught by our team of expert musicians/tutors. Lessons take place during the school day and cater to all experience levels, from beginners to advanced musicians. Students have the opportunity to showcase their progress in school concerts, gaining valuable performance experience.
We are particularly encouraging applications for orchestral string instruments (violin and cello), as well as brass and woodwind, as these currently have no waiting lists—meaning your child is very likely to secure a place straight away! With subsidised fees and priority placement for GCSE and A level music students, we strive to make music education accessible to all. Funding is also available for PP students. More information on how lessons work and where to apply will be available in September.
Music Clubs
Music Clubs are published in the Extra-Curricular Activities sheet and displayed on the music noticeboard.
QPCS Open Mic - Room P104, 3.00-4.00pm Run by students, for students; this is like a mini concert that happens twice every half-term!
If you play an instrument, or sing, come over for a little jam session! No parents or carers, very relaxed and informal. This is a chance for you to get more involved in the music scene at QPCS and a place to showcase your talent. There is no structure to this afternoon - if you have a song you have been practising and just want to play/sing it, you can! This is also a great opportunity to collaborate with other musicians in the school. All year groups welcome! Date of next session will be published in the QP Newsletter and displayed on the music noticeboard.
Calendar of Music Events at QPCS
Dates of Music Events are published in the school calendar.

pageCache.pageTitle: Home Learning - Queens Park Community School
pageCache.text:
Home Learning
Homework is set regularly. The emphasis on homework is a significant factor in our students’ academic success and parents/carers are asked to involve themselves in this aspect of the school’s work.
Homework timetables are issued to students in Years 7 to 11 to help them organise and plan their work. A copy of this timetable can be found near the front of their Homework Diary. The purpose of the homework timetable is to make a suggestion about how workload can be organised.
Homework is recorded by students in their homework diary and by teachers in Google Classroom. Our Google Classroom site enables students to access support and submit work.
Students’ responsibilities:
Complete their homework to a high standard
Read regularly
Parents’ & Carers' responsibilities:
For further information regarding homework, how much and often and expectations, please read our Home Learning Policy.
Encourage wider reading

pageCache.text:
QPCS Library
& Recommended Reading Lists
At QPCS we put an emphasis on literacy skills and expect every student to have a reading book with them at all times. The more regularly your child reads, the more literacy skills will improve.
Inside your child's school diary is a reading record to monitor their progress and a list of KS3 key words that year 7, 8 and 9 students will need to understand and spell in order to make good progress across the curriculum. Do encourage your child to read frequently and regularly at home. Ensure they complete their reading record and it would be particularly helpful if you made time to test them on the spelling and meaning of their key words. In addition to homework, your child should be reading 30 minutes a day.

Remote Education
Google Classroom - How to log in
Remote Education Provision: Information for Parents & Carers
This information is intended to provide clarity and transparency to pupils, parents and carers about what to expect from remote education.
Circumstances where it might not be possible for pupils to receive in person education fit into 2 broad categories:
The remote curriculum: what is taught to pupils at home
A pupil’s first day or two of being educated remotely might look different from our standard approach, while we take all necessary actions to prepare for a longer period of remote teaching.
What should my child expect from immediate remote education in the first day or two of pupils being sent home?
Students should expect to log into Google classroom immediately where they will find tasks.
Following the first few days of remote education, will my child be taught broadly the same curriculum as they would if they were in school?
We teach the same curriculum remotely as we do in school wherever possible and appropriate. However, we have needed to make some adaptations in some subjects. For example, in the practical subjects such as PE.
Remote teaching and study time each day
How long can I expect work set by the school to take my child each day?
We expect that remote education (including remote teaching and independent work) will take pupils broadly the following number of hours each day:
Key Stage 3 (Years 7-9)
Key Stage 4 (Years 10-11)
Key Stage 5 (Years 12-13)
A minimum of 5 hours per day. Depending on the number of courses being followed, more time may be required to complete all the work set.
Accessing remote education
How will my child access any online remote education you are providing?
The main resource is Google Suite for Education. In addition, students may be directed to other websites such as GCSEpod, Hegarty Maths, Educake Seneca etc. We have a "Continuous Learning page" which includes links to the above and further resources which can support with learning at home should students finish their work early.
If my child does not have digital or online access at home, how will you support them to access remote education?
We recognise that some pupils may not have suitable online access at home. We take the following approaches to support those pupils to access remote education:
How will my child be taught remotely?
We use a combination of the following approaches to teach pupils remotely.
All students are not expected to follow their timings of the school timetable but will receive work for from the subjects they would normally have that day. Students can spread this work out to complete throughout the day to meet their needs. Some examples of remote teaching approaches being used include:
Parents, Carers (and students) need to make the school aware if there are resources their children need at home, for example art canvases for GCSE. They will be able to collect these from school.
Long-term project work and/or internet research
Engagement and feedback
What are your expectations for my child’s engagement and the support that we as parents and carers should provide at home?
Please see our distance learning tips.
How will you check whether my child is engaging with their work and how will I be informed if there are concerns?
Classroom teachers will work with families to ensure students are engaging with remote education.
Our systems of rewards apply to celebrate those achieving well remotely.
How will you assess my child’s work and progress?
Feedback can take many forms and may not always mean extensive written comments for individual children. For example, whole-class feedback or quizzes marked automatically via digital platformare also valid and effective methods, amongst many others. Our approach to feeding back on pupil work is as follows:
Teachers have been asked to provide feedback at least once per week for those subjects where the students have more than one lesson per week on their timetable. For single lesson subjects, feedback will be integrated into the programme of study. Online tools for assessment, might include use of any of the following:
Online tools for feedback:
Recorded video messages e.g. Loom recorded messages
Voice recorded messages e.g. Mote.
Additional support for pupils with particular needs
How will you work with me to help my child who needs additional support from adults at home to access remote education?
We recognise that some pupils, for example, some pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), may not be able to access remote education without support from adults at home. We acknowledge the difficulties this may place on families, and we will work with parents and carers to support those pupils in the following ways:
Distance Learning Tips for Parents, Carers and Students
The guidance below can help us all make the best of new and sometimes unfamiliar distance learning environments. It can help you be ready for some of the more practical aspects of learning from home.

Curriculum
All students study the national curriculum, which at KS3 includes: English, maths, science, history, geography and RE (taught as an integrated humanities curriculum), modern foreign languages (Spanish and/or French), design and technology, art and design, music, physical education, citizenship and computing. Students have a PSHCE lesson once a week which covers: citizenship, relationships, health and sex education.
In Year 9 students choose from a range of KS4 options which they take in Year 10 and Year 11, in addition to their core subjects of English, maths and science.
Curriculum Overview & Intent
If you would like further information, please contact the relevant Head of Faculty.
Everyone is proud of the inclusive culture. They celebrate diversity and never tolerate bullying.
